subject.title: Config-driven reply suffix (or beforeReply transform hook) for per-agent signatures

question: Should OpenClaw standardize model, delivering-harness, surface, and thread-state metadata on the existing outbound reply hook, or keep signature policy entirely in external plugins using the current payload transformation seam?
rationale: The existing hook covers outbound text rewriting, but publishing additional runtime metadata or a core per-agent setting would create a durable plugin/config contract that cannot be selected safely from this report alone.

options.title: Validate an external plugin first
options.body: Keep core unchanged while a plugin proves that the existing hook and plugin-owned state can implement the requested signature lifecycle; add a narrow SDK field only if that proof finds a concrete missing fact.

options.title: Add a stable hook metadata contract
options.body: Document and test the minimal runtime metadata needed by outbound plugins, without introducing a core reply-suffix config setting.

options.title: Add first-party reply-suffix config
options.body: Introduce a supported per-agent config contract only if maintainers want this formatting policy to be a core product feature rather than plugin behavior.

recommendation.title: Validate an external plugin first
recommendation.body: Keep core unchanged while a plugin proves that the existing hook and plugin-owned state can implement the requested signature lifecycle; add a narrow SDK field only if that proof finds a concrete missing fact.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a core-versus-plugin contract decision rather than a narrowly mechanical bug fix.
